They are massive, bumbling humanoids with brutish limbs and wiry blonde hair. They may spawn with a large tree trunk in their hand. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Coins|0star=20-29|1star=40-58|2star=80-100}} {{drop row|item=Troll hide|0star=5|1star=10|2star=20}} {{drop row|item=Troll trophy|0star=50%|1star=50%| 2star=50%}}}} == Spawning == {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones|Anywhere]] in [[Black Forest]] |limit=1|frequency=1|stars=After 2000 meters from the world center}} {{spawn row|type=Possible [[Spawn points|spawn point]] outside [[Troll Cave]]s in [[Black Forest]]|frequency=0}} {{spawn row|type=Possible [[Spawn points|spawn point]] inside [[Troll Cave]]s in [[Black Forest]]|frequency=0}} {{spawn row|type=During "The ground is shaking" [[Events|event]] after defeating [[The Elder]]|limit=2|frequency=6|stars=Yes, if a [[Love Potion]] is active. Otherwise, No.}} {{spawn row|type=[[Spawn zones]] in [[Black Forest#Alternative biomes|Troll Black Forest]]|limit=2|frequency=667|stars=Yes}} }} == Attacks and abilities == Trolls come in two variants: 1/3rd of Trolls are equipped with a log, while the others are unarmed. Unarmed Trolls have three attacks. === Punch === Leans back before swinging to attack the player in a 5-meter 45-degree horizontal arc (60 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 4 seconds when within 4 meters of a player. === Ground slam === Lifts both fists up before slamming them down into the ground (70 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This slam reaches 4.5 meters out in a 90-degree vertical arc, and can be used every 20 seconds when within 5 meters of a player. This effectively means that the Troll will punch five times before doing a slam, assuming that the player is always in range. When the slam hits anything, including the ground, it also creates a 3-meter area that deals 50 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 50 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 30 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage. This area damage is the same at every star level. === Throw === Throws a large boulder at players within 8–20 meters (50 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 60 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). The boulder travels at an initial velocity of 15 meters per second and can travel for 4 seconds before disappearing. It has a spread of 10–20 degrees. This has a cooldown of 10 seconds and can be disabled by standing close to the Troll. Log Trolls have two attacks. === Log swing (vertical) === Slams their log into the ground extending out 9 meters and spanning across 90 degrees (70 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 6 seconds when within 8 meters of a player. === Log swing (horizontal) === Swings their log from the side, creating a 10-meter 50-degree arc (60 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]], 100 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 40 Tier 2 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage). This attack can be used every 6 seconds when within 8 meters of a player. ==Strategy== {{For|strategies for defeating Trolls|Aggressive creature strategies#Troll}} * Among the largest enemies in ''Valheim'', Trolls have a physical strength that reflects their size. Ranged attacks with a Bow or Spear are best and kiting a Troll through dense areas of the forest is very effective, as they have large hitboxes that hinder their pathfinding. * Trolls employ massive yet slow attacks that are easy to avoid but very hard to block and parry. Using a [[Bone Tower Shield]] is effective at blocking most of its attacks, provided the player has sufficient health. ** "Pulling" the attention of a Troll and brandishing a tower shield while other players fire arrow volleys is an effective strategy. * Trolls will sometimes fall into deep ditches or pits, or more often, the large pit at a copper dig site. Their poor pathfinding often renders them stuck. ** If a Troll approaches a ditch that is sufficiently deep (at least 6 meters) and does not fall in, it will not willingly walk in. Unable to reach the player, it will stand still, glowering into the pit. After a few moments, it will turn its aggression towards any player structures it can reach. ** Alternatively, if the positions are reversed, standing atop the ledge of a pit allows for easy dispatch with arrows and spears. * Trolls can spawn with or without a tree trunk in their hand. A Troll equipped with a tree trunk has decidedly better range and destructive power than one that is not. == Notes == * A 1-star Troll has a pale green tint, and a 2-star Troll is tinted a ruddy red. * They are tall (7 meters) and can move along corridors 2 meters and wider. * The curative pollen ejected by [[Greydwarf Shaman]]s also heals Trolls, as they share a [[Factions|Faction]]. * They cannot jump or swim, but they will walk along the bottom of shallow water, sometimes getting a considerable distance from the shore. They can walk through shallow water faster than a player can swim. * All the Troll's attacks (except its rock throw) have a [[Damage#Terrain_damage|tool tier]] of 2, which allows players to use Trolls to harvest resources they are otherwise unable to attain at their current equipment level. Trolls are capable of knocking down and breaking apart [[Oak]] and [[Birch]] trees with their attacks, which is especially useful in the early game for obtaining [[Finewood]] without a [[Bronze Axe]] (or better). Trolls can also break [[Copper Deposit|Copper]] and [[Tin Deposit]]s (even with their rock throw attacks), which can allow the player to get [[Bronze]] before killing the first boss, [[Eikthyr]]. ** Additionally, Trolls lured into more hostile biomes will aggressively attack most creatures in that biome, due to them having different Factions. While Trolls are not such a good match for stronger enemies, such as [[Plains]] creatures, they are capable of destroying large numbers of [[Swamp]] creatures, leaving loot like [[Entrails]] and [[Bloodbag]]s in their wake for the player to collect * The [[Love Potion]] increases Troll spawn rate, star chances and alerts them. == Gallery == Valheim Mountain-Troll-2 ver0-79-10.jpg|Mountain Troll preparing to smash a Viking in Deep Forest Troll in-game.png Screenshot 2021-05-18 9.27.56 AM.png|Recently updated Troll visuals Trollinswamp.jpg|Infuriated Troll lashing out at enemies in swamp (new model) File:1 star troll.png|A 1-star Troll at night. File:Helpless.jpg|A Troll trapped and helpless in a defensive ditch. == Trivia == * In Old Norse sources, Trolls were assimilated to Jötnar, the giants from Norse mythology. Only in later Scandinavian folklore did they appear as separate beings. * During the alpha, Trolls in the Black Forest had brown skin covered by green moss, while Trolls in the Mountains had blue skin.https://archive.md/s5GAU#selection-903.0-903.13 * The trophy of the brown Troll from the alpha build can be spawned with the command "spawn TrophyForestTroll", and the current troll trophy with "spawn TrophyFrostTroll" * The alpha build Troll trophy can be placed on an [[Item Stand]], however, it is invisible. == Lore == {{Quote|The trolls of Midgard may be fading from your memory, as indeed they are from all the race of man. Few and forlorn, they crouch in damp caves and gnaw on the bones of the weak and foolhardy. The will of Odin has pushed them back into the dark places. But in Valheim they have flourished. It has been centuries since any in Midgard saw the great Trolls stamp flat the land and bring down the trees for joy. Look upon this great and noble sight, wanderers in a strange land! Then take to your heels and run...|[[Runestone]]}} == References == {{Creatures}} [[ru:Тролль]] [[uk:Троль]] [[fr:Troll]] [[cs:Troll]] [[de:Troll]]

File:2Star Greydwarf.png|2 star Greydwarf == Notes == * The word Greydwarf is derived from Astrid Lindgren's tale Ronja the Robber's daughter (Ronja Rövardotter). Originally named Grådvärgar, which is literally translated to Greydwarves. They are short creatures with grey fur who will attack a person when they sense the victim's fear. If you are emotionally aggressive then they will leave you be. == Lore == {{Quote|Let all who read me beware of the Greydwarfs, the skulkers in darkness, the soulless ones. They are born from rot and rainfall, they spring like mushrooms from the smoking soil. There is nothing on their tongues or behind their eyes, those who fear nothing should still fear them. When the soul of a murderer or a great sinner rots under the ground, it makes a hollow cyst which draws rock and wood and moss to it. It gathers up the peat into flesh, braids reeds into bone and takes rags for skin. It should not walk but when the night comes it walks. Should you who read this see one with a sword to your hand, lance it and let it out. Or put it to the torch, for it fears the flame.|[[Runestone]]}} The runestones' portrayal of the Greydwarfs is racially motivated: they stereotype the entire race as "the skulkers in darkness, the soulless ones", with "nothing on their tongues or behind their eyes",In-game text, Greydwarf runestone ($lore_greydwarfs). and one urges travelers not to pity them: "Raised by the Old Man of the Forest from seeds of sin, the greydwarfs clothe themselves in the human forms they once knew, but there is no longer any warmth in their hearts. They live now only to serve the Elder and to protect the wood. Do not let pity for them stay your hand."In-game text, Black Forest runestone ($lore_blackforest_random09). == References == {{Creatures}} [[ru:Грейдворф]] [[fr:Naingris]] [[cs:Šedý trpaslík]] [[uk:Сіролюд]] [[de:Grauzwerg]] __NOTOC__

They are small flaming imps that are relatively weak, especially in [[Swamp]]s where the constant raining significantly reduces the damage from their ranged fireball attack. == Attacks and abilities == {{For|strategies for defeating Surtlings|Aggressive creature strategies#Surtling}} Surtlings spawning near [[Fire geysers]] can be farmed through lowering the ground around the spawn area with a pickaxe. As soon as the Surtling spawns in water, it will take damage and quickly die. === Fireball === Winds back before tossing a ball of fire at the player, which applies the [[Burning]] status (10 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 40 [[Damage types#Fire|Fire]] damage). This attack has a 3-second cooldown and can be used within 10 meters of a player. The fireball travels at 11 meters per second for up to 4 seconds before despawning and has a spread of 2–20 degrees. == Drops == {{drop table|{{drop row|item=Coal|0star=4|1star=8|2star=16}} {{drop row|item=Surtling core| 0star=50%|1star=2|2star=4}} {{drop row|item=Surtling trophy|0star=5%| 1star=5%|2star=5%}}}} == Spawning == {{spawn table| {{spawn row|type=3 [[spawn points]] near [[Fire geysers]]|frequency=Respawn after 5 minutes}} {{spawn row|type=During "There's a smell of sulfur in the air..." [[Events|event]] after defeating [[Bonemass]]|limit=4|frequency=6|stars=No}} }} == Notes == * Surtling is a reference to [[wikipedia:Surtr|Surtr]], also anglicized as 'Surt', a mighty giant fire jötunn in [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norse_mythology Norse mythology]. **Interestingly, in earlier versions of the game, among [[Runestone]]s the player may stumble upon in Swamp biome provided the origin of Surtlings as demonic creatures born from splintered fragments of Surtr himself after being struck down and mutilated by First Men. * The flames around 1-star Surtlings are blue, with 2-star Surtlings being pink. * Projectiles can be parried, staggering the Surtling for some time and allowing you to close the distance for melee attacks, and possibly pushing them into water. * While they take damage from water, rain does not affect them. * Before the [[Version history|Ashlands update]], Surtlings were very common and the only inhabitants of Ashlands. == Gallery == File:Valheim Surtling-1 ver0-79-10.jpg|

 == Lore == {{Quote|Let you who read me know of the Surtlings, that you might not fall prey to their wickedness. Long ago the great demon Surtr was brought down and destroyed by the First Men, giant warriors of whom you are but a dwindling echo. They smote long upon the body of this Surtr with swords and hammers so that his fiery substance was shattered into many small pieces. He who was made of the fire was fire in every part of him. You could not say ‘Here is the brain of Surtr’ or ‘Here is Surtr’s liver’ because every part was Surtr. So all the fragments of him were Surtr still, only much weaker in power and in thought and in memory, with no way to become whole once again. Now we call these fragments Surtlings and when they are found they should be stamped out like the last embers of a fire or doused with water to choke off their flames at the root. They will throw fire from afar and joy in causing terror and destruction. Even in his scattered dotage, the demon seeks revenge on the children of the First Men.|[[Runestone]]}} {{Creatures}} [[ru:Суртлинг]] [[uk:Вогневик]] [[fr:Surtling]] [[cs:Surtling]] [[de:Surtling]]

This attack has a 4-second cooldown and can be used within 20 meters of a player. == Gallery == Draugr archer.jpg Draugar roaming the swamp Valheim.jpg ==Notes== *Entering a [[Sunken Crypts|Sunken Crypt]] and leaving Draugr alive there will count towards spawn caps effectively suppressing their spawns in a large area. *[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Draugr Draugr] or Draug - "the undead of ''[[Valheim (world)|Valheim]]''", also called ''aptrganga'' or ''aptrgangr'' in the Norse literature. Draugr live in their graves, often guarding treasure buried with them in their burial mound. == Lore == {{Quote|Long ages ago, the world of Valheim was home to a race of proud and noble people. They built great towers that touched the clouds and delved deep into the earth for precious metals. But their pride was their undoing. They challenged the very gods and went to war against the Aesir and the Vanir, destroying themselves completely. Great Odin levelled their cities and Loki consumed their mines in fire. Mighty Thor broke down their towers and Freya sowed their fields with salt tears. Now they are sunk many hundreds of years deep. No songs sing of their stories, and the earth has claimed their cities. But pride cannot be killed entirely and the warriors who fought in that final battle will not surrender until their bodies are dust and the dust long gone. They return as Draugr, unholy walkers in ancient armour, creatures of rust and despair. Break them, bury them, let them know they are dead.|[[Runestone]]}} {{Creatures}} [[fr:Draugr]] [[cs:Draugr]] [[ru:Драугр]] [[uk:Драуґр]] [[de:Draugr]]

'''Bonemass''' is the third [[Creatures#Bosses|boss]]. He appears as a gigantic humanoid mass comprised of toxic ooze, mud and skeletal remains, likely absorbed from nearby tombs situated close to his altar.

== Summoning ==
[[File:BonemassAltar.png|left|thumb|200x200px|Bonemass' Forsaken Altar.]]
Bonemass' [[Forsaken Altars|Forsaken Altar]] is located in [[Swamp]]s. His location can be found when visiting [[Sunken Crypts]] and sometimes ruined structures, where a [[Runestone#Vegvisir|Vegvisir]] will reveal his nearest summoning location on the map.

He is summoned by placing 10 {{Item Link|Withered Bone}}s in his Forsaken altar in Swamps. Like all bosses, Bonemass can be summoned as many times as desired, provided the required materials are met.

== Attacks and abilities ==
{{For|strategies for defeating Bonemass|Boss strategies#Bonemass}}
Bonemass has an environment aura that forces raining, which means pulling him from the area cannot be used to remove [[Wet Effect|Wet]].

=== Area of effect ===
Bonemass will charge up with a thick green cloud before vomiting a wave of poisonous ooze, inflicting the [[Poison]] status on everything in a 9-meter radius around him (130 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage). This is signaled when he leans backwards. The poison cloud persists for 15 seconds and will continuously refresh the poison duration on any player that stays inside. This effect cannot be dodged or blocked. Bonemass can use this ability when a player is within 15 meters, and it has a cooldown of 30 seconds. The cloud is centered on the impact point of Bonemass's vomit; due to the size of his collision box, this results in the cloud not reaching very far behind him which gives players a safe area to retreat to that is still within range to strike him.

=== Punch ===
A close-range swipe at a player dealing up to 80 [[Damage types#Blunt|Blunt]] and 50 [[Damage types#Poison|Poison]] damage to players, in addition to 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Chop|Chop]] and 1000 Tier 0 [[Damage types#Pickaxe|Pickaxe]] damage to any trees or rocks hit. This attack can be used every 7 seconds when a player is within 8 meters. It hits in a horizontal 8.5-meter 66.1-degree arc in front of Bonemass.

=== Throw ===
At 50-second intervals, Bonemass will reach into his armpit to throw out a glob of goop in the general direction of the player at an initial velocity of 20 meters per second with a spread of 5–20 degrees. On impact, this ability will attempt to spawn four random monsters ([[Skeleton]]s and/or [[Blob]]s, with equal chances for both). A maximum of eight summons of each type can be active at once; but the selection of enemies each spawning instance is still random regardless of the status of spawn caps, meaning reaching the spawn cap for one type of summon will not force spawns for the other. Bonemass will still attempt to summon creatures even if both spawn caps are reached. This ability can only be used when a player is within 30 meters.

== Aftermath ==
Defeating Bonemass provides the player with a Wishbone, which allows the player to easily locate [[Silver Vein]]s beneath the surface of [[Mountain]] biomes (as well as buried [[Muddy Scrap Pile]]s in Swamp biomes, and other miscellaneous buried treasures in certain locations).

=== Forsaken power ===
Mounting Bonemass' trophy upon his respective stone will allow the player to claim his Forsaken Power. This ability will grant the player and nearby allies the following effects for 300 seconds:

* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Blunt
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Slash
* Damage modifier: [[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] vs Pierce
* Block stamina usage: -100%
* Block stamina return: +5

See [[Forsaken_power#Bonemass Power|Bonemass' power]] for more details.

=== Events ===
Defeating Bonemass affects the following [[events]] for that world:

* Disables: Draugr and Skeleton "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: Blobs and Oozers "A foul smell from the swamp..."
* Enables: "A skeleton surprise!"
* Enables: "A cold wind blows from the mountains." (if [[Moder]] has not been defeated)
* Enables: "There's a smell of sulfur in the air." (if a [[Surtling]] has died)
* Enables: "You are being hunted."
* Enables: "You stirred the cauldron." (if a [[Bat]] has died)
* Enables: "You feel a chill down your spine..."
Note: Two of these events unlock flying enemies that will be uninhibited by base walls and will attack tame animals. For example, bats will quickly wipe out any outdoor tame Boars (if the player has them), most likely before the player can swat them all. Therefore, in order to protect any rare animals (such as a 2-star [[Boar]]), it is advisable to build a secure indoor barn area before undertaking Bonemass.

=== Creature spawning ===
Defeating Bonemass unlocks [[Skeleton]]s to spawn at night in the Meadows, Black Forest, Swamp (additional), Mountain and Plains. They can only have 0 stars.

'''Forsaken powers''' are unlocked by defeating each boss and hanging their trophy on the [[Sacrificial Stones]]. By default, the player's set forsaken power is activated by [[Controls|pressing F]]. Only one forsaken power can be set at a time, which is changed out at the Sacrificial Stones.

All forsaken powers have a duration of 5 minutes. They also share the same 20-minute cooldown, which does not reset or reduce even when the player logs off, changes their active forsaken power, or sleeps.  

Activating a power locks the player into an animation for a couple of seconds. The player is unable to move or perform any action (with the exception of equipping or unequipping tools/weapons). 

When activating a forsaken power, all players within 10 meters will also receive the benefit of the forsaken power activated. Thus, a party of four players can keep a forsaken power activated virtually indefinitely by consecutively using each player's forsaken power.

{{Quote|The grace of the mighty stag flows through you. Your ability to move around is improved, be it on land or in water.}}
60% reduced [[stamina]] usage for running, jumping, and swimming.

{{Quote|The power of the forest invigorates you. You shall gather its bounties faster, just as you shall regain your own vitality should you lose it.}}

[[Resistance|Slightly resistant]] (-25%) VS pierce, slash, and blunt damage, -100% [[block]] stamina cost, +5 stamina returned per block.

==[[Moder]] Power==
{{Quote|The dragon's wings urge you on. You shall always have tailwind while sailing, and you shall swiftly carry heavy burdens, even over the coldest mountains.}}
Always tailwind when sailing, +300.0 increased [[carry weight]], +10% increased movement speed, [[Resistance|Resistant]] (-50%) vs frost.

*This power changes the [[wind]] direction while sailing, but not wind intensity. A calm wind will not aid in travel as much as a fast wind.

*This power is best saved for when there is headwind since crosswind (perpendicular to travel direction) and tailwind are about equally good for sailing.
*This power will not affect the wind if you are too close to the [[World Edge|World's Edge]].
